guide.importExport: Download saves the preset with all unsaved changes as a JSON file. Import opens such a file as a draft. Saving the draft replaces a preset with the same name.
guide.intro: The AR overlay shows rank, name, and time directly on the lanes of the camera image, following the perspective of the camera. The editor defines where the lanes appear in the image. The preset stores the lanes relative to the image, so it fits every browser source with the aspect ratio of its reference resolution.
guide.presets: A preset describes where the lanes appear in the image of one camera position. Each preset has its own AR overlay, whose address is listed on the dashboard.

shortcuts.lock: Lock or unlock the selected lanes
shortcuts.nudge: Move the selected lanes by 1 pixel
shortcuts.nudgeLarge: Move the selected lanes by 10 pixels
shortcuts.shiftSelect: Click with Shift, Ctrl, or Cmd held to add a lane to the selection or remove it. Drag on the empty canvas to select every unlocked lane it touches.

steps.1: Create a preset with the number of lanes, or choose an existing one. A preset belongs to one camera position.
steps.2: Set the aspect ratio and the resolution of the browser source and load a snapshot of the camera image, for example from the streaming software, as background image.
steps.3: Drag the corners of lane 1 and of the last lane exactly onto the lanes in the image.
steps.4: Use "Align lanes" to distribute the lanes in between, then correct single lanes if needed. Lock finished lanes so they are not moved by accident.
steps.5: Set the lane order and the camera position to match the image.
steps.6: Save. An AR overlay that is already open picks up the preset once it is reloaded.

guide.view:
These aids only exist in the editor and are not part of the preset.

The grid and the rulers show the pixels of the reference resolution, lines show the coordinates of the pointer while dragging. With magnets, dragged corners snap onto the corners and edges of other lanes and the image border. Without such a target nearby, edges and centers line up with those of other lanes and of the image, and a line shows the alignment. Holding Ctrl or Cmd places freely. The preview shows every lane as the AR overlay draws it. While a corner is dragged, a loupe magnifies the area around it, which the toolbar can switch off. A click on a ruler places a guide across it that follows a drag: the top ruler places vertical guides, the left one horizontal guides. Lanes snap to guides. A guide disappears when it is dragged back onto the ruler or double-clicked, all of them through the eraser in the toolbar. While moving, lines with measures show the distances to the neighbors, and even distances snap.

A background image, for example a snapshot of the camera image from the streaming software, makes it easier to trace the lanes. It fills the canvas and is kept in this browser for each saved preset, but never uploaded. Its opacity can be set in the toolbar.

The align menu lines up the selected lanes at an edge or a center line, or spaces them evenly. A single lane is aligned with the image.

The list of the lanes hides a lane for editing or locks it. With several lanes selected, position and size move and scale them together.

help.alignLanes: Distributes the lanes evenly between the top edge of lane 1 and the bottom edge of the last lane, following the perspective of the camera. Place lane 1 and the last lane exactly on the image first. Locked lanes keep their position.
help.frameSize:
The aspect ratio and the resolution of the browser source in the streaming software. They set the shape of the canvas and the pixels shown in the editor. The preset stores the lanes relative to the image, so the AR overlay fits every browser source with the same aspect ratio. Changing the resolution keeps the lanes in place in the image.

While the aspect ratio is locked, the height follows the width and the width follows the height.
help.lane:
The four corners of the lane in pixels of the reference resolution. Drag the corners by their handles or enter them here. Lanes drawn in red are dented, twisted, or mirrored and are not shown in the AR overlay.

A locked lane cannot be moved, is skipped by the marquee selection, and keeps its position when aligning.
help.laneCount: The number of lanes the camera shows. It cannot be changed later.
help.laneGap: The gap between two lanes in percent of the height of a lane, which aligning keeps. Changing it distributes the lanes again at once, as long as lane 1 and the last lane span a valid outline. Locked lanes keep their position.
help.laneOrder: Selects which lane of the heat is the top lane in the camera image. In the editor, the top lane is always lane 1.
help.textAnchor: Selects on which side of the lane rank, name, and time start. With "Right", the content runs from right to left.
help.textSize: Height of the text in percent of the height of a lane. The width of the content follows the shape of the lane in the image, so the text keeps its proportions.
